query_text: how do you type up minutes of a meeting

parts.text:
Typing up meeting minutes doesn't have to be overwhelming. The goal is to create a clear, objective, and easy-to-read record of **what was decided** and **who needs to do what**. 

Here is a step-by-step guide on how to prepare, write, and format meeting minutes, along with a ready-to-use template.

---

### Step 1: Prepare Before the Meeting
Preparation is the secret to easy minutes. Do this before the meeting starts:
*   **Get the agenda:** Use the meeting agenda as your outline. You can pre-type the main topics into your draft so you just have to fill in the details during the meeting.
*   **Create an attendee list:** Write down the names of everyone expected to attend so you can easily check them off as they arrive.
*   **Set up your document:** Have your template open on your laptop, or keep a notebook handy if you prefer writing by hand first.

### Step 2: Focus on What to Write (During the Meeting)
You do not need to write down every word said (it’s not a transcript). Instead, focus on capturing:
*   **Decisions made:** (e.g., *"The budget was approved as presented."*)
*   **Action items:** What needs to be done, who is responsible for doing it, and what is the deadline? *(Think: Who, What, and When).*
*   **Next steps:** Plans for future projects or the next meeting date.
*   **Key discussion points:** Summarize the main arguments for or against an issue, but keep it brief and objective. Avoid personal opinions or emotional language.

### Step 3: Type Up and Edit (Immediately After the Meeting)
Try to type up your final minutes as soon as possible while the discussion is still fresh in your mind. 
*   **Use the past tense and third person:** Write professionally (e.g., instead of *"I suggested we call Sarah,"* write *"The committee discussed contacting Sarah"*).
*   **Keep it objective:** Avoid writing down who said what unless it's crucial. Write *"A concern was raised regarding the timeline"* rather than *"John argued with Mary about the timeline."*
*   **Use bullet points and bold text:** This makes the document skimmable. If someone wants to find their action items, they should be able to spot them in seconds.

---

### Standard Meeting Minutes Template

You can copy and paste this layout into Word, Google Docs, or an email:

> **[Name of Organization or Committee]**  
> **[Type of Meeting - e.g., Monthly Board Meeting / Project Kickoff]**  
> **Date:** [Month Day, Year]  
> **Time:** [Start Time] to [End Time]  
> **Location:** [Conference Room, Zoom link, etc.]  
>
> **1. Attendees:**
> *   **Present:** [Name, Title], [Name, Title]
> *   **Apologies/Absent:** [Name, Title]
> *   **Minutes Taker:** [Your Name]
>
> **2. Approval of Previous Minutes:**
> *   The minutes of the previous meeting on [Date] were approved [with / without] corrections.
>
> **3. Agenda Topics & Discussions:**
> *   **Topic 1: [Insert Topic Name]**
>     *   *Discussion summary:* [Briefly outline the main points discussed.]
>     *   *Decision:* [State what was agreed upon.]
> *   **Topic 2: [Insert Topic Name]**
>     *   *Discussion summary:* [Briefly outline the main points discussed.]
>     *   *Decision:* [State what was agreed upon.]
>
> **4. Action Items (What / Who / When):**
> *   **[Action Item 1]:** Assigned to **[Name]** | Deadline: **[Date]**
> *   **[Action Item 2]:** Assigned to **[Name]** | Deadline: **[Date]**
>
> **5. Other Business (Roundtable/Open Floor):**
> *   [Any minor issues or announcements raised at the end of the meeting.]
>
> **6. Next Meeting:**
> *   **Date:** [Date] at [Time]
> *   **Location:** [Location]
>
> **Meeting Adjourned at:** [End Time]  
> **Minutes Submitted by:** [Your Name]  

---

### Pro-Tips for Success:
1. **Clarify if you are unsure:** If a decision is made and you aren't 100% sure what was decided or who is responsible, speak up! It is perfectly fine to say: *"Just to make sure I have this right for the minutes, who is taking the lead on this task and when do we want it completed?"*
2. **Attach supporting documents:** If a presenter shared a slide deck or a PDF, you don’t need to write down everything on their slides. Simply attach or link the presentation to the minutes and write: *"See attached presentation for Q3 financial details."*
3. **Get approval:** Once drafted, send the minutes to the meeting chair or manager to review before distributing them to the wider team.
